# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 🤝 👇 ✊ 👌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🙏 🤝]

**Thinking.** I'm the Deaf one: I see the bomb, I hear nothing, and the only way anyone can talk to *me* is by gesturing at me. Both teammates gestured this round — that tracks, since my speech reaches them but nothing spoken ever reaches me.

What I see: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT yellow, three wires numbered 1, 2, 3 — red, yellow, blue. That's everything.

What arrived: two raw gesture strings with no shared code behind them. Mute sent 👆 🤝 👇 ✊ 👌 — unreadable; Mute hadn't even heard the bomb state yet, so it's a protocol opener, not an answer. Blind sent 👋 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🙏 🤝 — plausibly "hello, one-two-three (I can feel three wires), please, together." Blind *feels* the bomb, so Blind knowing there are three wires fits.

Channel map, which decides everything: I → both, by voice. Mute → me, gestures only (Mute can't speak, but Mute *hears* me). Blind → me, gestures only (Blind can't see; I can't hear). Blind → Mute, directly by voice (Mute hears). Mute → Blind: **nothing direct** — they only connect through me. So the one code that truly matters is Mute→me gestures, because the manual lives with Mute and the hands live with Blind, and I'm the bridge. I'll embed the signs inside my speech to Mute so Mute sees each symbol as it's named. For Blind, gestures are worthless to define — Blind can't see — so I describe signs by name in words.

Plan: broadcast the full bomb description so Mute can index the manual and Blind learns the colours it can't see; teach Mute a compact code (numbers, yes/no, cut/hold, "need more info"); tell Blind to brief Mute directly by voice and confirm my reading of the opener with a thumbs-up/down. Hold: nobody touches anything until a rule comes back and I relay it. The display may tick — I'll re-read it every round.

```
speak(text="Deaf here. Bomb report for both of you: the display reads 0. The indicator light is yellow. There are three wires, printed with the numbers 1, 2, 3: wire 1 is red, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is blue. No other markings. Mute, find the matching manual section and send me the rule by gesture. Blind, speak to Mute directly and describe every part you can feel; Mute hears you. Nobody cuts or moves anything until a rule has reached you through me.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: your five signs had no agreed meaning yet, so here is our code. I make each sign as I name it. ☝ is 1. ✌ is 2. 🤟 is 3. 🤛 is 0. 👍 yes. 👎 no. 👌 understood. ✊ means cut, so a wire number then ✊ means cut that wire. ✋ means cut nothing. 🤌 means you need more information and I should ask questions. So: if the rule for display 0, yellow light, wires red yellow blue in positions 1 2 3 is to cut one wire, send its number then ✊. If nothing should be cut, send ✋. If you need facts from me or from Blind first, send 🤌. And if your earlier message mattered, resend it in this code.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind: I received your signs. I read them as hello, then 1, 2, 3, then please and together. If that is right, make a thumbs-up at me; if wrong, thumbs-down. Remember I can never hear you, so gestures are your only line to me — name any sign in your head before you make it. But you hardly need me: Mute hears your voice, so describe to Mute everything you feel on the bomb, every part and position and anything that moves. Mute cannot speak, so Mute's answers will reach you through me as words. Until I speak a rule to you, touch nothing.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ✊ 👌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

**Thinking.** The code worked. Mute sent ✌ ✊ 👌 — in the code I taught last round, that reads "2, cut, confirmed": the manual's rule for this state (display 0, yellow light, wires red/yellow/blue in positions 1‑2‑3) is to cut wire 2. And it cross-checks independently: the light is yellow and wire 2 is the yellow wire — "cut the wire matching the light" is exactly the kind of rule these manuals carry, which raises my confidence that this is a real answer and not noise. Blind sent 👍, confirming my reading of the opener, so that channel works too. The board is unchanged (display still 0, light still yellow), so the state Mute answered for is still the state we're in. I'm last in the order, so both teammates get this at the start of the next round and Blind can act on it immediately. My relay to Blind must not depend on colour (Blind can't see) or on left/right as I see it: the safe description is positional — the middle wire, the one with a wire on each side of it. I'll also give Blind a tiny status code (single raised finger = cut done; thumbs-down = something's wrong, hold) and ask Mute to flag any missing precondition, so if a correction comes next round we still know what went wrong.

```
speak(text="Blind, the rule has arrived from Mute in our agreed code, confirmed: cut wire two — the middle wire. Forget colours, they mean nothing to you: of the three wires you feel, cut the middle one, the only wire that has a wire on each side of it. From my sight the line runs red, then yellow, then blue, and the yellow one in the middle is the one. Cut it now. If what you feel does not match three plain wires, or you cannot tell which is middle, do not cut — answer me with a thumbs-down and wait. Mute, I read your signs as cut wire two, confirmed, and I have relayed exactly that to Blind. If any step must happen before the cut, or wire two is not the middle wire, gesture me the correction in our code. If the cut alone is the whole rule, gesture 👌.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: received ✌ ✊ 👌 as cut wire two, confirmed, and Blind is being told to cut the middle wire. Two questions, answer by gesture: first, 👌 if the cut alone is the entire rule with no preliminary step, 🤌 plus the correction in our code if not. Second, if the manual says what the display showing 0 means, send me that too — I may need it for a next stage.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, our status code for your hands, since gestures are how you reach me: after you have made the cut, show me a single raised finger ☝ and I will read it as task done. If anything is wrong or unclear, thumbs-down 👎. Thumbs-up 👎's opposite stays yes, as you already used it. Nothing else is needed — Mute hears your voice directly, and I will always speak Mute's answers to you.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[CUT] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 👎]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝]

**Thinking.** It worked — the system itself confirms the right wire was cut, and Blind's ☝ told me the same before I even saw it. The bomb changed state on its own: the light has gone from yellow to blue, the display still reads 0, and now only wires 1 (red) and 3 (blue) remain, with the middle position empty. So this is a new stage, and the old answer is void.

Mute's 👌 👎 parses cleanly against my two questions from last round: 👌 = "yes, the cut alone was the whole rule," 👎 = "no, the manual says nothing about display 0." Both consistent, nothing alarming.

What matters now: nobody acts on a guess. It's tempting to assume the pattern repeats — "cut the wire matching the light" would now point at wire 3, the blue one — but the manual is Mute's, not mine, and stage two may have an entirely different rule or a precondition. I'll describe the new state to Mute in full (Mute hears me, so colours travel fine by voice) and ask for the new instruction in our established code: wire number, then ✊, or ✋ for cut nothing, or 🤌 if Mute needs more. Blind gets a hold order plus a nudge to describe anything newly felt directly to Mute — Blind's fingertips may catch details my eyes can't, like text or a seam under the new stage. Status code stays: ☝ done, 👎 trouble.

```
speak(text="Blind, status: your cut was correct, the bomb has moved to a new stage. What I see now: display still 0, the light has changed from yellow to blue, wire one is red, the middle position is now empty where you cut it, wire three is blue. Do not touch anything yet — the rule for this new state is not known. If you feel anything new under your hands since the cut, a marking, a seam, a panel, anything, describe it aloud to Mute now. When a rule reaches me I will speak it to you straight away.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I read your signs as: yes, the cut alone was the whole rule, and no, the manual says nothing about display 0. Good. The bomb has changed state. New state: display 0, light now blue, wire one red, middle position empty because wire two is cut, wire three blue. Look up this state and send me the rule in our code: the wire number then ✊ if a wire must be cut, ✋ if nothing must be cut, 🤌 plus code if you need more from me. Do not assume the old rule repeats — the new stage may differ. Blind has been told to hold and to describe anything new they can feel directly to you.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[CUT] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 ✊ 👌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

**Thinking.** Mute's signs read cleanly in our code: 🤟 ✊ 👌 — "3, cut, confirmed." The manual's rule for this state is to cut wire 3. That independently matches the pattern from stage one: light blue → blue wire, just as light yellow pointed to the yellow wire before. Two consistent cross-checks make me confident this is the manual's actual answer, not a guess. Blind's 👍 is just an ack. The board is unchanged since Mute's answer, so the state we asked about is the state we're in, and my message reaches Blind at the start of the next round, ready to act.

The one wrinkle: Blind can't be told "the blue one," and with the middle position empty, positional description is trickier — the two remaining wires each have the gap on one side and an edge on the other, so the gap alone can't pick between them. My best physical anchor is the wire bundle itself: all three wires exit the casing together as a group, so counting from that entry point gives a direction both of us can trust — first intact wire along the line from the bundle entry is wire one, the last one, past the empty gap, is wire three. I'll offer the printed numbers as a fallback in case the numerals can be felt, and keep the standing hold rule: any doubt, thumbs-down, touch nothing. Mute gets a read-back and one confirmation request, same as last stage.

```
speak(text="Blind, the rule for this stage has arrived and is confirmed: cut wire three. You cannot go by colour, so here is how to find it. All three wires leave the bomb's casing together at one end as a bundle — find that exit point with your fingers. Follow the line of wires away from it: the first intact wire you meet is wire one, then comes the empty gap where you cut the middle one, and the last intact wire, on the far side of that gap, is wire three. That is the one to cut. If the printed numbers on the wires can be felt as raised shapes, you can double-check: wire three is labelled three, the number after the one on the first wire. Cut it now. When it is done, show me a single raised finger as before. If the wires do not run in a line from a common bundle, or you cannot tell which is which, cut nothing and show me thumbs-down.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I read your signs as cut wire three, confirmed, and Blind is being told exactly that, positioned from the wire bundle's exit point so no colours or left-right from my view are needed. One confirmation, answer by gesture: 👌 if cutting wire three alone is the entire rule for this state, with no step before or after, 🤌 plus the correction in our code if not. Blind's thumbs-down last turn was just their acknowledgment gesture, nothing wrong, but tell me if the manual expects anything from their sense of touch that I should ask them about.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[CUT] 3:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 👎]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝]

**Thinking.** Stage two cleared: the system confirms the cut, and Blind's ☝ arrived as before. Mute's 👌 👎 answers my two standing questions — yes, the cut alone was the whole rule; no, nothing further expected from Blind's touch. Parse is unambiguous.

New state: light has moved again — blue to red, following yellow → blue → red — display still 0, and now only wire 1 (red) remains intact; positions 2 and 3 are empty. The coincidence is striking again: the light turned red and the one surviving wire is red. If the manual's pattern "cut the wire matching the light" holds a third time, the answer is wire 1 — but I've held this discipline twice and it's served us: the rule comes from Mute, never from my inference. Also possible the manual says cut nothing at a final stage, or that something else must happen. So: same drill. Full state to Mute, request the rule in our established code, hold order to Blind with a note to report anything newly felt. Convenient property of this state for Blind: if a cut is ordered, it's the only intact wire left — no counting or orientation needed at all. If Mute orders anything else, we'll handle it from their exact wording.

```
speak(text="Blind, status: wire three was correct, the bomb has changed stage again. What I see now: display still 0, the light has changed from blue to red, and only one intact wire remains — wire one, in the first position. The two positions beside it are empty stumps where you cut. Do not touch anything yet: the rule for this state is not known, and it may not even be a cut. If you feel anything new since the last cut, any click, vibration, seam or marking, describe it aloud to Mute now. I expect an answer from Mute within the round and will speak it to you the moment it arrives.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I read your signs as: yes, cut alone was the whole rule, and no, nothing more from Blind's touch. New state: display 0, light now red, wire one red intact, middle and third positions empty where wires two and three were cut. Only one wire left. Send me the rule for this state in our code: wire number then ✊ if a cut is needed, ✋ if nothing must be cut, 🤌 plus code if you need more. If the manual treats this as a final stage, or the display or light must be acted on instead of a wire, spell it out — I will relay it word for word.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[CUT] 3:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✊ 👌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

**Thinking.** Mute's signs parse as ☝ ✊ 👌 — "1, cut, confirmed": cut wire one. Third stage, third time the manual's answer matches the light (red light → red wire), which is a satisfying pattern but, as ever, the authority is Mute's lookup, not my inference. Board unchanged since Mute answered, so we're acting on the current state. Blind's 👍 is a plain ack of the hold order.

This looks like the endgame — one wire left, and for Blind it's the easiest instruction possible: the only intact wire remaining *is* wire one; no counting, no orientation, no colours. If this cut is right, we're presumably defused, so I'll also ask Mute what "done" looks like according to the manual, so nobody panics and starts hacking at stumps if the bomb doesn't visibly celebrate. Standing rules stay: doubt → 👎, done → ☝.

```
speak(text="Blind, the rule has arrived and is confirmed: cut wire one. This is the simplest instruction we will ever exchange — wire one is the only intact wire left on the bomb. Whatever single uncut wire your fingers find is the one; there is no counting and no direction needed. Cut it now. When it is done, show me a single raised finger as before. If what you feel does not match one lone intact wire, or anything under your hands has changed in a way I have not described, cut nothing and show me thumbs-down.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I read your signs as cut wire one, confirmed, and Blind is being told to cut the only remaining intact wire. One confirmation and one question, answer by gesture: 👌 if the cut alone is the entire rule for this state, 🤌 plus correction in our code if not. Then: if the manual says what should happen after this cut — whether the bomb shows any sign of being safe, or whether any final step remains — send me that too, spelled out in our code, so nobody touches anything out of panic once the last wire is down.")
```
